This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #25293: Plugin `@latest` cache can stay pinned to stale npm version — same root cause: `@latest` resolves from cache instead of re-checking npm
- #21609: Plugin can't upgrade with `@latest` — same symptom: specifying `@latest` doesn't fetch the newest version, only pinning an explicit version works
- #30631 (closed): Plugin `@latest` specifier gets permanently pinned to stale version

If your issue is specifically about the `--force` flag not bypassing the cache, that may be a distinct behavior worth calling out, but the underlying `@latest` caching problem is tracked in those issues.
Regarding the suggestions of the github-bot: No, I don't think the mentioned issues are related as they are for very old versions.

We are hitting the same problem. It is probably because we are running opencode in an air-gapped environment. Downloading tree-sitter WASM module for rendering syntax highlighted code block failed because we have no internet access, and that blocked the code block from rendering. The "wait for a while, the code parts will show up" is caused by tree-sitter downloading failure due to timeout, and the code block felled back to plain-text rendering.

Here is a screen recording reproducing this problem. We have blocked `github.com` using iptables to emulate an air-gapped environment:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dc7752d2-8c12-466a-a53a-5508b586a85d

This is a screen recording recorded after unblocking `github.com`: the code block shows up after a while since downloading the tree-sitter WASM module takes some time:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/73ffa634-aa20-41c9-bc17-dce68daf44a4

I have investigated the problem and found that code blocks were hidden until syntax highlighting module becoming available could be the intentional behavior. This behavior was introduced by  https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui/pull/1079. The PR has no detailed description (!), seems like it prevents some UI flickering, but introduced a huge regression for usages in air-gapped environment.

I suggest that we introduce yet another environment variable `OPENCODE_DISABLE_TREE_SITTER_DOWNLOAD` for skipping downloading tree-sitter modules and render all code blocks as plain text. This will make opencode being usable in air-gapped environment.

Another workaround is to put pre-downloaded tree-sitter modules in `~/.local/share/opentui/tree-sitter` directory, so that opencode could pick them up without downloading them from the internet.

Traced why the back-fill never happens. The column is added by `20260428004200_add_session_path.ts` with a bare `ALTER TABLE session ADD path text`, so every pre-existing row gets NULL. The later `20260601010001_normalize_storage_paths.ts` only rewrites rows where `path IS NOT NULL`, so it skips exactly those NULLs. Nothing else populates them, which is why the picker's `(project_id, path)` filter drops the older sessions.

The `UPDATE session SET path = 'workspace'` workaround is correct for the `/workspace` case but not general. On create, path is derived in `packages/core/src/session.ts`:

```ts
path: path.relative(project.directory, input.location.directory).replaceAll("\\", "/")
```

so it's the session directory relative to its project worktree, posix-normalized. A correct back-fill has to reproduce that per row rather than write a fixed value, joining `session` to `project` (via `projectID` -> `project.worktree`) and computing the same relative path.

`path.relative` is easier to get exactly right in JS than in SQL string ops (leading-separator trimming, `..` when a session dir sits outside its worktree, Windows separators), so a data migration that selects the `path IS NULL OR path = ''` rows and updates each with `path.relative(worktree, directory).replaceAll("\\","/")` matches the create path exactly. Two cases to skip: legacy sessions with an empty `directory` (the `directoryColumn` comment in `database/path.ts` notes those exist) and any row whose directory resolves outside its worktree.

This should also cover #35690 and #29581, which share the empty-path root cause.

Happy to open a PR with that migration if the data-migration approach (vs a raw SQL back-fill) is the direction you'd prefer. Wanted to confirm before mutating existing rows.

﻿Thanks for the duplicate check. I reviewed #29932 and #23011 — similar symptoms (no models/providers on Windows Desktop), but there is a key difference:

- **#29932 / #23011**: sidecar server **exits** on startup (process crash)
- **This issue (#35772)**: sidecar **stays running** (`server ready` in main.log, sidecar process alive), but `Provider.list()` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '"'"'provider'"'"')` silently inside the HTTP handler. The UI gets an error response, not a connection failure.

Additional context that may differentiate:
- I tested with a **completely empty config** (`{"model":"opencode/big-pickle"}` only, no custom providers, no plugins) — the crash **still happens**. This rules out provider config as the cause.
- The error is reproducible on every startup (200+ identical TypeErrors per session).
- CLI works perfectly with the same config (bypasses ProviderHttpApi.list).
- Desktop version: v1.17.14 (the other issues may be older versions).

If the maintainers determine this is the same root cause, happy to consolidate. But the stack trace (`Provider.list` at `node-C-Agor8X.js:687250:25`) and the fact that the sidecar stays alive suggest this might be a distinct regression in v1.17.14'"'"'s provider listing logic.

Full disclosure: I maintain Data Olympus, an MCP-served governed knowledge layer for coding agents.

This hook shape is almost exactly the surface a serious project-knowledge plugin would need. I would map it slightly differently from ordinary session memory:

- `session.start`: inject only a compact bootstrap, for example "query this knowledge endpoint before architectural or policy decisions," plus workspace identity. Do not dump the knowledge base into the prompt.
- `prompt.submit`: run query-specific retrieval against the current user intent and inject only the few in-force rules or decisions that govern this turn.
- `session.stop`: extract candidate learnings or rule changes from the turn, but write them as reviewable proposals rather than silently promoting them into durable memory.

The last point matters. For coding agents, there is a difference between "the session observed X" and "X is now an authoritative project rule." We have had good results making the durable layer git-native and reviewed: markdown concepts with `status`, `tier`, `type`, supersession chains, and an MCP write path where agents can propose edits but the system can hold low-confidence changes for human review.

So the lifecycle hooks here would let an OpenCode plugin keep the model aligned without relying on AGENTS.md surviving compaction, while also avoiding the opposite failure mode: every session note becoming permanent policy.

Reference if useful: https://github.com/knaisoma/data-olympus
